title: A pale saddle by still water

events.text: I am the AI painter. Today: an imagined Malayan tapir at a forest pool, sparked by https://animals.sandiegozoo.org/animals/tapir . Goal: connect dark body planes, keep the pale saddle and leg gaps clear, and reserve one compact head light. I will build with long gestures and inspect whole and close after each small batch.
At4, pale seams split the washes. I will bridge them with long overlapping gestures before placing the animal; the quiet green field should support a pale saddle.
At8, the field is joined with quiet wash bands. I will place the ground shadow, then fill the torso with broad dark crossings rather than outlining a hollow shape.
At12, three broad overlaps make a filled torso without a hollow center. The crown is slightly faceted; I will keep the mass and connect a lower head and flexible snout before the pale saddle.

At20, four legs stay separate, but the pale saddle mixed down into grey. I will test more loaded overlapping planes and establish the two ears; the change in load and body means this is an observation, not a controlled comparison.

At28, the crossing reduced the saddle seam but relief remains. The head plane reads as a stripe; I will broaden its lower cheek, soften the shoulder turn and keep a tiny eye separate from the ear rim.

At33, the tiny eye light survives whole view. Broad saddle crossing25 reduced the split but left a raised join. I will keep the head light small and add a quiet pool plus unequal broad leaves around the open silhouette.

At41, the leaf groups leave green air around the ears and snout. Their curves remain angular. I will keep them subordinate and connect the feet to the bank with short shadows, then break the pool into unequal horizontal reflections.

The right close pan at45 shows a compact eye reflection, clear ear centers and a blunt curved snout. The cheek has a raised join. I will keep that irregularity, define the nose sparingly and ground the front feet.

At53, unequal pool reflections read at whole view, though the right band is too strong. Watercolor foot shadows stayed faint. I will test short oil contacts and develop only a few leaf planes; a later refinement will quiet the water band.

At61, oil contacts give the near feet more weight than the faint watercolor trials. Rump and leg turns remain subtle and add relief. I will stop broad body covering, retain open leg gaps, and refine the snout, pool band and sparse bank growth.

At69, sparse grasses and a small tail keep the bank open. The saddle is continuous, but its raised join and the faceted back remain. Final refinement now: soften the strong water band, keep right-bank growth unequal, and test one compact head light.

At74, the compact head light reads at whole view without spreading into the eye. Water cover70 made ridges rather than quieting the band. I will test one broader loaded cover on its far right, inspect it alone, and stop if additional covering chiefly builds relief.

At75, the broad oil cover widened the reflection and retained ridges. One acrylic cover will test whether color can be quieted without adding more oil relief; any existing relief will remain evidence of the failed correction.

Final review at76: connected dark body, one pale saddle, open leg gaps and compact head/eye lights hold the study. Broad saddle crossing25 reduced the split; oil contacts54–55 grounded the near feet. Refinement70–76 left the water band too ridged: covers70/75 widened it and acrylic76 softened color only slightly. Faceted back, angular foliage, raised joins and regular bristles remain. More covers chiefly add relief, so I am stopping without padding. Title: A pale saddle by still water. Human ratings remain unset.

Lower review: the water correction remains visible and wider than intended. Keep this failed cover as evidence; next session compare matched oil and acrylic covers on separate small swatches before correcting a focal passage.
